In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the growth of single- to few- layer graphene is possible on stainless steel substrated using alcohols as a carbon source.
the presence of FeO in the steel substrate is essential for the rapid growth of single-layer and few-layer graphene.

the growth of graphene on stainless steel is not limited by the carbon source, but rather the elemental composition of the stainless steel itself, and that the growth of high quality single-layer graphene can be achieved by using aliphatic alchols as the carbon feedstock.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
single layer graphene can be grown on stainless steel with high growth rate, but the growth rate is dependent on the chemical composition of the substrate.

single-layer graphene growth is possible on stainless steel substrata, and the presence of Fe, Cr, and Mn species in the stainless steel substrate has a significant influence on the quality of graphene growth.
the presence of Cr and Mn is detrimental for graphene growth on stainless steel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the growth of graphene on stainless steel is rapid (less than one hour at 1000 °C) compared with the growth of graphene using conventional CVD techniques on copper foils (12-24 hours at 900-1050 °C).
the growth of graphene on stainless steel can be tuned to produce single- to multi-layers of graphene, depending on the choice of carbon source.
the use of stainless steel substrates can be an inexpensive alternative to the more expensive copper foils for the growth of large-scale graphene.
